done.why: I was just getting somewhere, with a trident in hand and a pump by a lake, when the world told me I'd used all 30 turns it allows. I'd have kept going a bit longer; I wasn't bored yet.

about: Breaking into an empty white house, dropping through a trap door into caves, and grabbing treasure while things with axes try to stop you. A classic dungeon crawl, but someone has shaken it: the trap door gets barred behind you, the Round Room's passages are caved in, and touching the mirror makes the earth rumble.

moments.note: Someone bars the trap door behind me as I go down. Who? That was a nice jolt and I had no way back.
The troll fight is a dice roll. Six turns of 'attack troll with sword' is a lot for an impatient person; I almost gave up and wandered off.
'It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head' and the black fog eating the body. Worth the slog, barely.
Round Room 'passages in all directions' but several caved in, and it doesn't say which. I just had to guess a direction.
'There is an ugly person staring back at you.' The game insulted me and I laughed.
Touching the mirror made the earth rumble and the room shake but the description was identical afterwards. Something happened and I don't know what.
Poseidon's own crystal trident lying on the shore. First real treasure, and it felt earned after the troll.
Hit the turn cap with a pump in reach and a lake in front of me. Cut off right as it got interesting.

wished: I wished the Round Room told me which passages were caved in instead of making me guess.
I wished the troll fight was over faster, or that there was some trick to it besides swinging six times.
I wished I'd found out what the mirror rumble actually did.
I wished I could have taken the pump and tried the lake before the turns ran out.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Told me I wasn't alone and there was no going back. That's the moment I stopped being a tourist.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: The payoff for six turns of swinging. The sinister fog eating the carcass afterward was a good touch.

lines.line: Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.
lines.why: This is where it was clear the place had been changed; the hub room was no longer a hub.

lines.line: There is an ugly person staring back at you.
lines.why: Made me laugh out loud. A game that insults you is a game with personality.

lines.line: There is a rumble from deep within the earth and the room shakes.
lines.why: Mysterious and unresolved; it's the thing I most want to go back and figure out.

lines.line: On the shore lies Poseidon's own crystal trident.
lines.why: First treasure. Made the whole descent feel like it was going somewhere.

fun.why: The house break-in and the descent were brisk and fun, and the treasure find was a good hit, but the troll fight ate a fifth of my turns on repeated identical commands.

engagement.why: I kept wanting the next room. The barred trap door and the mirror rumble both hooked me, and I was annoyed to be cut off at the cap rather than relieved.

difficulty.why: Nothing stumped me; the only hard part was the troll, and that was luck not thought. The caved-in Round Room was more unclear than hard.

interestingness.why: The changes from what I half-expected (barred door, cave-ins, the rumbling mirror) made me curious about what else was different. The Atlantis Room was a nice reveal.

prose.why: Terse and dry with real wit: the ugly person in the mirror, the troll with an axe to grind, the curtains line. Room descriptions are plain but clear.
